 --> 8th Pay Commission: CPI inflation breaches 6%; will it strengthen demands for higher fitment factor?
 Whether higher inflation will translate into a more generous pay revision under 8th CPC remains uncertain, as the Commission will also have to consider the government's fiscal position and the broader economic outlook. 
 Dipen Pradhan 
 November 16, 2026 / 16:53 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Retail inflation crossed 6% in October 2026.
 Unions demand higher fitment factor under 8th CPC.
 Fitment factor is not directly linked to inflation.
 Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery

 Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE 
 As India’s retail inflation increased to 6.09 percent in October 2026, crossing the RBI’s upper limit of 6 percent, it has strengthened the case for central government employees’ demand for better salaries and pensions under the Eighth Pay Commission .  
 Various employee unions and federations have demanded a fitment factor ranging from 3.0 to 4.38 under the 8th CPC, as compared with 2.57 under the Seventh Pay Commission. 
 However, whether higher inflation will translate into a more generous pay revision remains uncertain, as the Commission will also have to consider the government's fiscal position and the broader economic outlook. 
 Further, financial and legal experts highlight the distinction between the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and the All-India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW). While CPI measures retail inflation and guides the RBI's monetary policy, AICPI-IW is used to calculate Dearness Allowance (DA) revisions for central government employees. 
 Could CPI inflation crossing 6% strengthen demand for a higher fitment factor?

 According to Rohitaashv Sinha, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, rising inflation could strengthen employee unions' arguments before the 8th Pay Commission, particularly because lower-paid employees and pensioners are more vulnerable to increases in essential expenses. 
 "Unions will use this number, and they have a fair point to make. Retail inflation came in highest in two years, driven by food inflation. Food eats up most of a junior employee’s monthly budget, so a jump like that hits the person at Level 1 far harder than someone at the top of the pay scale. Pensioners, who live on a fixed amount, feel it too," Sinha said. 
 The National Council-Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM) has demanded an increase in minimum basic pay from Rs 18,000 to Rs 69,000, based on a fitment factor of 3.833. They are also seeking a change in the family-size assumption used to calculate minimum pay. 
 Read more : NC-JCM pushes for 5-unit family model, minimum pay of Rs 69,000 
 Higher inflation does not translate into a higher fitment factor 
 "Inflation doesn’t change what the unions are asking for. What it does is give them a stronger story to tell the Commission and the public. Whether that turns into a higher fitment factor is another matter, since the Commission will also look at what the government can afford," Sinha said. 
 He added that the Commission would consider longer-term inflation trends, existing DA levels and the financial implications of a salary revision rather than relying on a single month's CPI reading. 
 “ Dearness allowance already exists to offset rising prices, and it reached 63 percent in July 2026. That is why a single month’s CPI reading is unlikely to move the Commission on its own. It will look at longer-term price trends, the DA trajectory and the cost to the exchequer," Sinha said. 
 Fitment factor not directly linked to inflation 
 Although both CPI and AICPI-IW measure price changes, they serve different purposes. CPI tracks changes in the prices of goods and services consumed by households and is used by the RBI to assess retail inflation and frame monetary policy. 
 AICPI-IW, on the other hand, measures price movements based on the consumption patterns of industrial workers. It is used to calculate DA revisions for central government employees to compensate for changes in their cost of living. 
 Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, explained that the two indices have different coverage and purposes, while the fitment factor is determined through a broader assessment. 
 "CPI tracks price changes across the goods and services a typical household buys. AICPI-IW is narrower, built specifically around what industrial workers spend, which is why it is the number used to revise Dearness Allowance for central government employees," Shetty said. 
 He further explained that the fitment factor is not directly linked to monthly inflation readings or routine DA calculations. 
 "The fitment factor is different. It is a one-time multiplier set when a new Pay Commission comes in, decided through a broader review of pay levels and affordability, not through regular inflation tracking. Inflation plays a role only as background context for that review, not as a direct input into the number itself," he added. 
 While higher CPI inflation can strengthen the argument for better compensation, AICPI-IW remains the relevant index for DA revisions. For September 2026, the index stands at 155.5 points, up 1.1 points from August 2026. 
 The 8th Pay Commission was constituted on November 3, 2025, and is expected to submit its report approximately 18 months later, or in the first half of 2027. The report will subsequently be examined by the Finance Ministry and the Cabinet before the government takes a final decision.
